architecture_posture.stance: Zero-runtime registry. The published artifact is `public/r/*.json` plus committed `.tsx` sources — never an importable npm package.
architecture_posture.rationale: Constraint 6 plus verified prior art: `expo-ai-elements` reserved the npm name and shipped tarballs containing 2-3 files and zero component code (`files:['src/']` pointing at a non-existent dir, `main:'expo-router/entry'`). Every `import ... from 'expo-ai-elements/...'` in its own README is unresolvable. If we publish an npm name at all it must be a pointer package that errors loudly on import, or nothing.

architecture_posture.stance: RNR is consumed as a peer registry by full URL, not vendored and not reimplemented. Our `registryDependencies` point at `https://reactnativereusables.com/r/uniwind/<name>.json`.
architecture_posture.rationale: Constraint 1. 29 of 55 shadcn deps already exist in RNR at 32/32 engine parity. Vendoring them would fork the design system and break constraint 3 (one visual system). The known cost — RNR can change what a URL serves — is mitigated by a scheduled CI job that reinstalls the example app from the live registry and typechecks, not by vendoring.

architecture_posture.stance: This library ships zero theme files. No `global.css`, no `@theme` block, no `tailwind.config.js`, no `lib/theme.ts`, no `NAV_THEME`, no ThemeProvider, no color literal anywhere in the tree.
architecture_posture.rationale: Constraint 5. The only way a consumer override passes through with no per-component wiring is if we never declare a token — we only *consume* utility classes that Uniwind resolves in the consumer's own Metro pipeline. Any value we hold is a value the consumer cannot override.

architecture_posture.stance: Presentation only. No transport, no `useChat`, no streaming client, no tool executor, no persistence ships in the registry. Components are prop-driven and stateless about the model.
architecture_posture.rationale: AGENTS.md already declares this split. It also keeps `ai` out of the install graph so a consumer on LangChain, their own hook, or a raw SSE reader can use the components. The AI SDK is wired exactly once, in `apps/example`.

architecture_posture.stance: Uniwind-only for v1, with the RNR dual-engine directory layout in place from commit one (`packages/registry/src/uniwind/...`).
architecture_posture.rationale: See distribution_design.tradeoff. Deferring Nativewind is a build-script fan-out plus a Tailwind v3/v4 utility-name pass later, not a rewrite — because we never call `cssInterop`/`withUniwind` ourselves; RNR's `Icon` absorbs the one genuine engine divergence.

architecture_posture.stance: Expo Go-safe core; every native-module capability is an opt-in registry item with the dev-client requirement stated in its `description`.
architecture_posture.rationale: Constraint 7. `react-native-enriched-markdown` ships a `codegenConfig` with Fabric components (verified on the npm manifest) and is absent from Expo SDK 57's `bundledNativeModules.json` — it cannot run in Expo Go. If `message-response` hard-binds to it, the entire chat shell becomes dev-client-only. Making the markdown renderer an injected prop keeps ~45 of 49 components Expo Go-runnable for a 3-line cost.

architecture_posture.stance: `Conversation` is virtualized from day one — `FlatList` with `inverted` + `maintainVisibleContentPosition`.
architecture_posture.rationale: Prior art's `Conversation` is a `ScrollView` + `.map()` wearing FlatList-shaped props. It renders every message, passes every code review, and degrades with usage. This is the single defect most worth not inheriting.

architecture_posture.stance: Verification is tiered by what the tool can actually observe: Vitest owns pure logic, type-conformance, and build scripts; a device/simulator tier owns render, style, portal, inset, animation, and theming.
architecture_posture.rationale: Uniwind compiles classes in the Metro transform. Even a perfectly working React Native render under Vitest cannot assert a single style, because the styling engine is not in the Vitest pipeline. Scoping Vitest to what it can prove is the honest architecture, not a concession.

architecture_posture.stance: Every string goes inside RNR `Text`; every icon goes through RNR `Icon as={...}`; every class merge goes through RNR `cn` imported from `@/lib/utils`.
architecture_posture.rationale: These three indirections are what make constraint 3 (one visual system) and constraint 5 (theming passthrough) mechanically true rather than aspirational. `Icon` is also the one file where Nativewind and Uniwind diverge, so routing through it is what keeps our source engine-agnostic.

architecture_posture.stance: Overlays inside our own `sheet`/`command` use a NAMED `PortalHost`, designed at plan time — not the root default host.
architecture_posture.rationale: An RNR `Select` or `DropdownMenu` rendered inside a bottom sheet portals to the root host and appears *behind* the sheet. This is invisible on web and only reproduces on device.

system_components.name: packages/registry/src/uniwind/components/ai/*.tsx
system_components.role: The 49 ported AI Elements components. The product. Import RNR by alias (`@/components/ui/*`, `@/lib/utils`) so the build script can retarget paths on install.

system_components.name: packages/registry/src/uniwind/components/ui/*.tsx
system_components.role: The 16 base primitives we own because RNR does not ship them (sheet, slider, table, toast, toaster, item, empty, field, input-group, button-group, spinner, command, breadcrumb, kbd, sidebar, navigation-menu). Written to RNR's exact file shape — `cva` + `cn(variants, contextClass, className)` + `Platform.select` — so a consumer cannot tell ours from RNR's.

system_components.name: packages/registry/src/examples/*.tsx
system_components.role: Runnable demo compositions published as `registry:example` items (chat shell, agent trace, tool-approval flow). Doubles as the docs code samples so samples cannot rot.

system_components.name: packages/registry/registry.json
system_components.role: shadcn registry index. One entry per item: `name`, `type`, `title`, `description`, `dependencies` (npm), `registryDependencies` (FULL URLs only), `files[{path,type,target}]`.

system_components.name: packages/registry/scripts/build-registry.ts
system_components.role: Reads `registry.json` + sources, rewrites internal `@/registry/uniwind/...` imports to consumer aliases, emits `public/r/<name>.json` and `public/r/registry.json`. Deterministic — byte-identical output for identical input, so the CI freshness gate works.

system_components.name: scripts/check-registry-fresh.ts
system_components.role: CI gate (`registry` job in AGENTS.md). Re-runs the build into a temp dir and diffs against committed `public/r/`. Fails on stale output. Also asserts every `registryDependencies` entry starts with `https://` — the short-name form silently resolves against the shadcn WEB registry and installs DOM components.

system_components.name: scripts/check-tokens.ts
system_components.role: CI gate. Greps registry sources for `#rrggbb`, `rgb(`, `hsl(`, `oklch(`, and `style={{ color:` and fails on any hit. This is the deterministic enforcement of the theming-passthrough contract; without it, drift is only visible on a device in a rebranded app.

system_components.name: apps/example (Expo 57 + expo-router + Uniwind)
system_components.role: Dev harness, device verification target, and — via `expo export -p web` — the docs site that also hosts `public/r/*.json` once a domain exists. The ONLY place `ai` / `@ai-sdk/react` appear.

system_components.name: apps/example/app/api/chat+api.ts
system_components.role: A real expo-router API route calling a real provider with `streamText` + `toUIMessageStreamResponse()`. Exists specifically so streaming, throttling, auto-scroll, and tool-state rendering are verified against a real token stream — the prior-art repo verified against a `setTimeout` simulation and that is not evidence.

system_components.name: vitest.config.ts + tests/
system_components.role: Logic tier: markdown part-serializer, tool-status to badge mapping, attachment media categorization, throttle scheduler, build-script output. Plus the type-conformance test against AI SDK v7. No component rendering.

system_components.name: Device verification protocol (apps/example + simulator/emulator)
system_components.role: The tier that owns everything Vitest structurally cannot: portal layering, safe-area insets, keyboard behavior, Reanimated transitions, streaming under real jitter, and the token-flip theming proof in light AND dark on iOS and Android.

system_components.name: .github/workflows/ci.yml
system_components.role: Jobs: typecheck (tsgo), lint (biome ci), test (vitest run), registry (freshness + URL-form gate), tokens (hardcoded-color gate). Plus a scheduled job that installs the example app fresh from the live RNR registry and typechecks, to catch upstream RNR drift.

gap_resolution.notes: Path trails in file-tree / sandbox / web-preview headers. ~35 lines. Horizontal ScrollView instead of web's wrap-and-ellipsis, since a phone bar overflows before it wraps. Publishes TextClassContext 'text-sm text-muted-foreground' so the trailing crumb can override to 'text-foreground'.

Segmented row for controls / toolbar / message actions. A `flex-row` View plus a small context that publishes corner-radius overrides to first/last children (RN has no `:first-child`). Do NOT try `[&>*:first-child]:` — descendant selectors are web-only and compile to nothing.

Building a month grid is the wrong answer on mobile — the OS picker is the platform affordance and users already know it. Not a registry item; documented in the example app where a date is actually needed. react-day-picker is DOM-only regardless.

Embla is DOM-only. Attachment galleries and image strips are a horizontal paged FlatList — one prop, zero dependencies, correct momentum physics for free. Used inline inside `attachments`/`image`, not shipped as its own item.

Recharts is DOM+web-SVG. No component in the 49 needs a plotted chart on mobile: `test-results` needs a progress bar (RNR Progress) and `package-info` needs counts (Text + Badge). RNR's own scope excludes components requiring third-party libraries beyond @rn-primitives; a charting surface would violate that. If one ever appears, it belongs in the consumer's app on victory-native, not in this registry.

cmdk is DOM+keyboard-first and has no mobile analogue. On device the command palette IS a bottom sheet with a filter field and a virtualized list. Backs model-selector, voice-selector, mic-selector. Critical: any RNR overlay opened from inside it needs a NAMED PortalHost mounted by the sheet, not the root host.

vaul's Drawer and shadcn's Sheet collapse to one component on mobile. Building both is duplicated gesture and Reanimated code with two sets of bugs. `drawer` is exported as a thin alias so ported AI Elements sources that reference Drawer keep compiling.

Icon + title + description + optional action slot. ~40 lines. This is `ConversationEmptyState` generalized, and it is also the fallback surface for file-tree, sources, attachments, and test-results. Build once, reuse six times.

Label + control slot + description + error text. Publishes 'text-destructive' via TextClassContext when `invalid`, which is how the error state reaches the description Text and its icon without prop drilling.

shadcn's Form is a react-hook-form + zod adapter. Neither is a UI concern and both are the consumer's choice. Every AI Elements surface that looks like a form (`prompt-input`, `environment-variables`, `confirmation`) is a controlled TextInput and needs no resolver. Shipping this would import a state library into a presentation registry.

Leading/trailing addons around a TextInput. The highest-leverage gap item — `prompt-input` is built on it, and so are the filter fields in command, attachments, and environment-variables. Must own the focus ring itself (`ring-ring/50` on the wrapper driven by onFocus/onBlur state), because RN has no `:focus-within`.

Nothing in the 49 AI Elements components takes a one-time code. It appears in the shadcn dep list because the upstream registry declares a broad common set. RNR's own `verify-email-form` auth block already covers this if a consumer needs it.

Generic media / content / actions row. Second-highest leverage after input-group: sources, file-tree, attachments, model-selector, queue, plan, and task all render lists of these. Publishes TextClassContext so title and description variants style without per-call classes.

~15 lines. Renders only where a hardware keyboard exists — gated on `Platform.OS === 'web'` by default with an `always` escape for iPad Magic Keyboard. Shows the submit hint in prompt-input. On a phone it renders null, which is correct rather than a compromise.

The primitive already exists and RNR simply has not wrapped it — so this is a styled shell (~70 lines) against RNR's template, not new behavior. Reuse-before-create makes it cheap enough to ship, but no component in the 49 requires it on a phone: schedule it in the last wave and cut it if the wave slips. Portal + contentInsets apply.
Numbered page controls are a desktop pattern. Long result sets (sources, test-results, queue) page in on scroll. No item shipped.

react-resizable-panels needs a pointer drag. Split views in canvas / panel / sandbox become Tabs on phone, and a detail bottom sheet where the panes are asymmetric. A gesture-handler drag divider is possible on tablet/web but is deferred — it is polish on a surface that already works.

Radix ScrollArea exists to replace the browser's scrollbar chrome. React Native has no scrollbar chrome to replace, and there is no `@rn-primitives/scroll-area` (confirmed absent from the npm scope). ScrollView *is* the scroll area. Every ported `<ScrollArea>` becomes a plain ScrollView with a `max-h-*` class.

from: RNR dialog as the styling template
gap_resolution.notes: The most load-bearing new component: backs drawer, command, sidebar (mobile), panel, open-in-chat, model-selector. Props: `side` (bottom|top|left|right), `snapPoints`, `dismissOnPan`. Must mount its own NAMED PortalHost so overlays opened inside it layer above it. iOS content wraps in `FullWindowOverlay` per RNR's dialog. Web renders without the pan gesture.

shadcn's own Sidebar already degrades to a Sheet below its mobile breakpoint — we ship that branch as the default and keep a persistent `View` column behind a width check for web/tablet. A SidebarProvider context carries open state and the collapsed/expanded rail width. Do not port the CSS-variable rail-width machinery; it is a `useState` on native.

from: RNR switch/progress as the styling template
gap_resolution.notes: Primitive exists, RNR has not wrapped it. Styled shell only. Needed by audio-player (scrubber), transcription (seek), voice-selector (rate/pitch), controls. Enlarge the thumb hit-slop well past its visual size — the web thumb size is not a touch target.

Sonner is a DOM toast library — it cannot be ported, only replaced. Every ported `toast()` call site maps onto our imperative `toast()` backed by @rn-primitives/toast. Listed separately from `toast` because the ported sources import from `sonner` by name and the build script must retarget those imports.

Deliberately NOT RN's ActivityIndicator, despite that being the platform affordance. ActivityIndicator takes a `color` prop and cannot read a Tailwind class, so it would be the one element in the library that ignores TextClassContext and visibly mismatches its surrounding button/badge — a direct hit on constraint 3. A rotating RNR Icon inherits color for free. Uses `reduceMotion: ReduceMotion.System` so it respects the OS accessibility setting.

Primitive exists, RNR has not wrapped it. Backs schema-display, test-results, package-info, environment-variables. Wrap in a horizontal ScrollView by default — a phone-width table with more than two columns needs horizontal scroll, and web's `table-layout` has no RN equivalent. Column widths are explicit flex values, not `auto`.

from: RNR alert as the styling template
gap_resolution.notes: Primitive exists, RNR has not wrapped it. Variants default/destructive/success, matching RNR's Alert palette so the two are visually one family. Respects safe-area insets on both edges — a toast at `bottom-0` sits under the home indicator.

The host plus the imperative `toast()` API — a tiny module-level queue store (`useSyncExternalStore`) and a `<Toaster />` that renders it. Explicitly documented to mount as a sibling of RNR's `<PortalHost />` in the root layout; mounted inside a screen it disappears on navigation. This is the one gap item with real state, and it is ~80 lines, not a library.

theming_mechanism.how: The library declares nothing and consumes everything. Every component styles exclusively through (1) RNR's semantic Tailwind utility classes — bg-background, bg-card, text-foreground, text-muted-foreground, bg-primary/text-primary-foreground, bg-destructive, border-border, bg-accent, ring-ring, plus rounded-sm/md/lg derived from --radius; (2) cva for variants with RNR's exact precedence cn(variants, contextClass, className) so a caller's className always wins; (3) cn imported from the consumer's @/lib/utils, never a local copy, so tailwind-merge conflict resolution is identical to RNR's; (4) TextClassContext.Provider on every container with a text intent, publishing a cva result exactly as RNR's Button does, so descendant RNR Text AND Icon inherit; (5) RNR's Icon as={...} wrapper for every single icon — never a raw Lucide component. We never touch NAV_THEME, ThemeProvider, or React Navigation chrome.
theming_mechanism.consumer_override_path: Consumer edits --color-primary (or any token) in THEIR global.css under @layer theme { :root { @variant light|dark { ... } } } -> Uniwind's Metro transform (withUniwindConfig) recompiles class-to-style mappings in THEIR bundle -> every bg-primary in every file the CLI copied out of our registry resolves to the new value on the next build. Zero props, zero context providers from us, zero per-component wiring, zero re-publish of the registry. It is exactly the same mechanism by which a consumer's override reaches RNR's own Button, because our components are the same kind of file in the same tree. Dark mode passes through identically: we emit no dark: variants of our own and no useColorScheme branch, so the consumer's @variant dark block drives our surfaces automatically. The two places a consumer needs a knob rather than a token — markdown node styles and the syntax-highlight palette — are exposed as required/optional props, not as internal constants.
theming_mechanism.failure_mode: Four ways to break it, all silent. (1) A hardcoded color anywhere. The prior-art repo's DARK_MARKDOWN_STYLE is a constant of hex literals inside message-content.tsx; every consumer who rebrands gets correctly themed chrome wrapped around off-brand markdown, and light mode is simply undefined — library defaults. Nothing errors. (2) Shipping our own global.css or @theme block: two sources of truth, and whichever loads last silently wins. (3) Inventing a token RNR does not define — bg-reasoning, text-tool-pending. Tailwind drops unknown utilities without warning, so the component renders unstyled on the consumer's machine while looking perfect in our example app, which happens to define it. (4) A local cn/clsx copy inside our tree instead of importing @/lib/utils: tailwind-merge stops deduping against the consumer's config and caller className quietly stops winning over our variants. Add a fifth for completeness: rendering a raw Lucide icon with a className — it is ignored with no error, so that one icon freezes at default color while its neighbours re-theme.
theming_mechanism.verification: Deterministic gate in CI: scripts/check-tokens.ts greps registry sources for #[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}, rgb(, hsl(, oklch(, style={{ color:, backgroundColor:, and any import of lucide-react-native outside icon.tsx; fails the build on a hit. Second gate: assert every --color-*/utility root used in our sources appears in RNR's published token set (parse reactnativereusables.com/r/uniwind/*.json once and cache), catching invented tokens. Device gate (the one that actually settles it): in apps/example, swap global.css for a deliberately loud alternate palette — magenta primary, high-contrast background, non-default radius — clear the Metro cache, rebuild, and screenshot the chat screen, an agent-trace screen, and a tool-approval screen on an iOS simulator AND an Android emulator in BOTH light and dark. Six screenshot pairs. Every pixel of every surface must move. Anything that does not move is a hardcoded value the grep missed — most likely inside a markdown or syntax-highlight style object.

repo_layout: package.json (private:true, pnpm workspace root) + pnpm-workspace.yaml + turbo.json
packages/registry/registry.json — shadcn registry index, hand-authored, one entry per item
packages/registry/src/uniwind/lib/*.ts — markdown part-serializer and other pure helpers, published as registry:lib
packages/registry/src/examples/*.tsx — runnable demo compositions, published as registry:example
public/r/*.json + public/r/registry.json — the BUILT, COMMITTED registry (this is the shipped artifact)
apps/example/ — Expo 57 + expo-router + Uniwind app: dev harness, device verification target, docs site via `expo export -p web`, and the only home of ai/@ai-sdk/react
.github/workflows/ci.yml — typecheck | lint | test | registry | tokens, plus a scheduled upstream-RNR drift job
distribution_design.registry_shape: Standard shadcn registry.json ($schema: https://ui.shadcn.com/schema/registry.json), name: 'rnr-ai-elements', homepage, items[]. Each item: { name, type: 'registry:component', title, description (states dev-client requirements when any), dependencies: [npm packages at Expo-pinned versions], registryDependencies: [ONLY absolute https URLs], files: [{ path, type, target }] }. Two hard rules enforced in CI: (a) every registryDependencies entry is an absolute URL — RNR deps as https://reactnativereusables.com/r/uniwind/<name>.json, our own intra-registry deps as https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hackerpug-ai/rnr-ai-elements/main/public/r/<name>.json. A short name like 'card' resolves against the shadcn WEB registry and installs a DOM component — the documented silent trap. (b) target is always set, so files land in components/ai/ and components/ui/ rather than wherever the CLI guesses. Base primitives we own target components/ui/ deliberately: they must sit beside RNR's own files so a consumer edits one directory, not two.
distribution_design.engine_variants: Uniwind only for v1. src/uniwind/ is in the path from the first commit so src/nativewind/ can be added later without moving a file or changing a target. Concretely, the Nativewind port would be: fan out the build script, run a Tailwind v3/v4 utility-rename pass (shadow-xs->shadow-sm, outline-hidden->outline-none, shrink-0->flex-shrink-0), swap the registryDependencies URL segment uniwind->nativewind, and re-verify on device. No component logic changes, because we never call cssInterop or withUniwind ourselves — RNR's Icon owns the only genuine engine divergence, and we consume it by alias.
distribution_design.tradeoff: Constraint 6 says distribute exactly like RNR, and RNR ships 32/32 nativewind/uniwind parity. Read strictly, that argues for dual variants on day one. Read as 'the same mechanism' — registry JSON, RNR CLI, copy-paste, files the consumer owns — Uniwind-only satisfies it. I recommend Uniwind-only, and here is the honest cost on each side. Dual costs 2x the registry surface (98 AI items + 32 UI items instead of 49 + 16), a 2x CI matrix, two device-verification passes per component, and a v3/v4 class-compat burden carried on every single PR forever — on a v1 that has 49 components to port and one maintainer. Uniwind-only costs: a Nativewind consumer cannot install today, and the class-compat debt is paid later in one batch instead of continuously. Three facts tilt it. RNR needs parity because it is the base layer everybody must be able to use; we are a layer on top and can require an engine the way any opinionated library requires a peer. The repo is already pinned Uniwind + Tailwind v4 by decision. And the deferral is genuinely cheap for the structural reason above. Name the trigger explicitly in the README so it is a decision and not a drift: add src/nativewind/ when the first real Nativewind consumer asks, or before tagging 1.0, whichever comes first. Second distribution call: host from raw.githubusercontent.com on main from day one — it is proven by prior art, needs zero infrastructure, and the item JSON is byte-identical when a custom domain is added later, so only the URLs in registryDependencies change.

expo_compatibility.go_vs_dev_client: Deliberately split. The CORE — conversation, message, message-content, prompt-input, suggestion, tool, reasoning, chain-of-thought, plan, task, agent, checkpoint, artifact, sources, citation, empty/spinner/shimmer, and every gap primitive we build — runs in EXPO GO, because it depends only on React Native core plus modules present in Expo SDK 57's bundledNativeModules.json (reanimated 4.5.1, worklets 0.10.1, gesture-handler ~2.32.0, svg 15.15.4, safe-area-context ~5.7.0, screens ~4.26.0). RNR itself is Expo Go-clean, so this preserves the base layer's property. A DEV CLIENT is required only for four opt-in capability items: markdown rendering (react-native-enriched-markdown — verified codegenConfig with Fabric components, absent from bundledNativeModules), streaming markdown (react-native-streamdown), speech input (expo-speech-recognition), and audio capture beyond expo-audio's Expo Go surface. This is why message-response takes an injected renderMarkdown prop with a plain-RNR-Text default: without that ~3-line seam, the single most important component in the library becomes dev-client-only. One universal install rule: always `npx expo install`, never npm latest. Several relevant packages have npm latest AHEAD of Expo 57's pin (gesture-handler 3.2.1 vs ~2.32.0, webview 14.0.1 vs 13.16.1, reanimated 4.6.0 vs 4.5.1, flash-list 2.3.2 vs 2.0.2, keyboard-controller 1.22.4 vs 1.21.9) and taking latest breaks the native build at runtime, not at install.

per_dependency.dep: react-native (FlatList, ScrollView, Pressable, TextInput, KeyboardAvoidingView, Platform, Linking, Animated)
per_dependency.notes: Core. Expo Go. The substitute target for scroll-area, carousel, pagination, resizable, and calendar-adjacent flows. Zero install.

Expo Go. expo install -> 4.5.1 (npm latest 4.6.0 — do not take it). Drives sheet, spinner, shimmer, reasoning/collapsible transitions. Always pair entering/exiting with reduceMotion: ReduceMotion.System.

Expo Go. Expo pin 0.10.1. Reanimated 4 peer. WARNING: uniwind x worklets form a mutual react-native shim cycle causing a startup stack overflow — prior art hit this on device and needed an outermost Metro arbitrator. Budget this as an example-app task, not a discovery.
Expo Go. Expo pin ~2.32.0 (npm latest 3.2.1 is a MAJOR ahead — taking it breaks the native build). Needed for sheet pan-to-dismiss, slider thumb, and RNR's scrollable Select.
Expo Go. Expo pin 15.15.4. Transitive under lucide-react-native.
Expo Go. Expo pin ~5.7.0. Required for toast/toaster edge placement, prompt-input bottom inset, and contentInsets on every anchored RNR overlay.
Expo Go. Expo pin ~4.26.0. Supplies iOS FullWindowOverlay, which sheet and dialog content wrap in.

Expo Go (JS over react-native-svg). NOT in bundledNativeModules so expo install falls through to npm — currently 1.39.0, while the RNR KB pins ^0.577. That is a MAJOR boundary with export renames; every icon import must be verified at whatever version is pinned. Always via RNR Icon as={...}, never rendered directly.

Expo Go. Pure JS/RN. Pin ALL @rn-primitives packages to one version (1.5.2) — mixed versions cause silent context mismatches between parts. slider/table/toast/navigation-menu/toolbar are published but unwrapped by RNR, which is what makes 5 of the 26 gap items cheap.
Expo Go. Build-time only (withUniwindConfig in metro.config.js, uniwind-types.d.ts). No native code. uniwind-types.d.ts is also what the RNR CLI sniffs to auto-serve Uniwind variants.

Expo Go. Pure JS, already RNR peers. Open question carried from the KB: whether tailwind-merge correctly dedupes Uniwind-specific utilities is still unverified upstream — worth a targeted Vitest case since it is pure logic.
Expo Go. Expo pin ~57.0.1. Powers copy buttons in code-block, terminal, stack-trace, snippet, message-actions.
Expo Go. Expo pin ~57.0.2. Send/stop/approval feedback in prompt-input and confirmation.

Expo Go. Expo pin 13.16.1 (npm latest 14.0.1 is a major ahead — do not take it). Sole dependency of web-preview and jsx-preview. Constraint-4 nuance: an iframe is banned, but a native WebView is the legitimate RN affordance for previewing a URL — a platform component, not a DOM construct.
Expo Go. Expo pin ~57.0.4. Backs the image and attachments previews with caching and content-fit that RN's Image lacks.
Expo Go for playback. Expo pin ~57.0.4. Backs audio-player and transcription playback. Recording permissions need a config plugin and therefore a dev build.
Expo Go. Expo pin 2.0.2 (npm latest 2.3.2 — do not take it). OPTIONAL, documented drop-in for very long transcripts. The shipped conversation uses core FlatList so the item carries zero dependencies.
Expo Go. Expo pin 9.1.0. The calendar substitute. Used in the example app only, not shipped as a registry item.

Expo pin 1.21.9, present in bundledNativeModules but Expo Go availability is NOT verified — treat as dev-client until proven. OPTIONAL for prompt-input; the shipped item uses core KeyboardAvoidingView so the default path stays dependency-free.

DEV CLIENT REQUIRED — this is the one that forces the split. Verified codegenConfig declaring Fabric components (EnrichedMarkdown, EnrichedMarkdownText, EnrichedMarkdownTextInput) for iOS and Android; absent from Expo 57 bundledNativeModules; peer-depends on katex. Installable via expo install + prebuild/EAS, so Expo-compatible — but NOT Expo Go. Ships as the opt-in message-response-markdown item. Requires flavor='github' for tables and $$...$$ block math.

DEV CLIENT REQUIRED (transitively). npm 0.2.0. Peers: react-native-worklets >=0.8.3 and react-native-enriched-markdown >=0.4.0. LANDMINE: its documented workletizableModules Metro option was renamed upstream to importForwarding.moduleNames; the stale key is SILENTLY IGNORED and crashes all markdown streaming on device. Peer of react-native-enriched-markdown. Pure JS. Only in the markdown item's dependency set.

DEV CLIENT REQUIRED. jamsch/expo-speech-recognition, versioned 57.0.0 to track the SDK but a community package with a config plugin, not first-party Expo. Opt-in dependency of speech-input / mic-selector / transcription only.

Pure JS, Expo Go fine. Deliberately NOT a dependency of any core registry item — declared only by the opt-in ai-sdk-adapter (registry:lib) and by apps/example. Requires expo/fetch for streaming on native; RN's global fetch does not stream response bodies. Do not repeat prior art's mistake of declaring it and never importing it.

api_endpoints.notes: This is a UI registry. It performs no network I/O, opens no sockets, and holds no credentials. It has no endpoints by design, and that is what keeps it usable with any AI backend.

expo-router API route (app/api/chat+api.ts). Calls a real provider via streamText and returns toUIMessageStreamResponse(). Exists so streaming, throttling, auto-scroll, and tool-state rendering are verified against a real token stream rather than a setTimeout simulation. Client side must use expo/fetch, not global fetch, which does not stream response bodies on native.
The distribution surface. Static JSON consumed by the RNR CLI. Not an application API; no auth, no rate-limit handling on our side.

technical_risks.risk: Vitest cannot render React Native components, and even if it could it cannot assert a single style. Uniwind resolves classes in the METRO transform; under Vitest a className is an inert string. So the failure is not one problem (Flow-typed RN source) but two stacked, and the second has no fix within Vitest.
technical_risks.mitigation: Scope Vitest to what it can actually prove and put a device tier under everything else. Cost to prove the render path, concretely: vitest-react-native is at 0.1.5 (0.1.x, thin ecosystem) or hand-roll a Flow-strip transform + react-native exports-condition resolution + transformMode.ssr + mocks for reanimated/svg/gesture-handler/uniwind. Optimistically a day; realistically several, with a permanently fragile config on RN 0.86/0.87 — and at the end of it, style assertions still do not work. Run this as its OWN first task with a hard timebox and a written go/no-go before any component work depends on it. Vitest's real and substantial scope: the AI SDK type-conformance test, the markdown part-serializer, the stack-trace parser, getMediaCategory, tool-status to badge mapping, the throttle scheduler, and the registry build/freshness/token scripts. Fallback if render tests are genuinely needed: add jest-expo@57.0.5 + @testing-library/react-native@14 as a SECOND runner for rendering only. Absolute floor: do NOT substitute a mock renderer and report the component as tested.

technical_risks.risk: Markdown rendering forces a dev client, and if message-response hard-binds to react-native-enriched-markdown the entire chat shell becomes non-Expo-Go, breaking constraint 7 for the library's most important component.
technical_risks.mitigation: Injected renderMarkdown?: (md: string) => ReactNode prop with a plain RNR Text default (~3 lines). Ship message-response-markdown as a separate registry item whose description states the dev-client requirement. Core stays Expo Go-clean. Verified basis: the npm manifest declares codegenConfig with Fabric components and the package is absent from Expo 57's bundledNativeModules.

technical_risks.risk: uniwind x react-native-worklets mutual react-native shim cycle causes a startup stack overflow — the app does not boot.
technical_risks.mitigation: Prior art hit this on device and needed an outermost Metro arbitrator. Budget it as an explicit task in the example-app scaffold, not as a debugging surprise. It blocks everything downstream, so it belongs in the first wave.

technical_risks.risk: react-native-streamdown's documented workletizableModules Metro option was renamed upstream to importForwarding.moduleNames. The stale key is silently ignored and crashes ALL markdown streaming on device.
technical_risks.mitigation: Already-paid discovery from prior art. Write the correct key, add a comment naming the rename, and verify streaming on a real device before claiming the item works. A config typo here produces no build error and no lint error.

technical_risks.risk: Repeating prior art's non-virtualized Conversation — FlatList-shaped props over a ScrollView + .map(). It renders every message, passes every code review, and only degrades with real usage.
technical_risks.mitigation: Build on core FlatList with inverted and maintainVisibleContentPosition from the first commit. Add a review check and a device test at 500+ messages. FlashList 2.0.2 documented as an optional swap, not the default, so the item stays dependency-free.

technical_risks.risk: Pin discrepancy between AGENTS.md and Expo's own resolver. AGENTS.md declares RN 0.87.1 under Expo 57.0.19, but Expo SDK 57's bundledNativeModules pins react-native: 0.86.3 and the Expo docs table says SDK 57 -> RN 0.86. Several npm latest versions are also majors ahead of Expo's pins (gesture-handler 3.2.1 vs ~2.32.0; webview 14.0.1 vs 13.16.1).
technical_risks.mitigation: Reconcile before scaffolding — one coherent set, resolved by npx expo install, never npm latest. Record the resolved pins in AGENTS.md and add a CI step running npx expo-doctor so drift fails the build rather than surfacing as a native crash. Second-order risk: @rn-primitives 1.5.2 is verified against RN 0.85.3 in the RNR KB, so its behavior on 0.86.x is untested by anyone and needs a device smoke pass across all portal components early.

technical_risks.risk: Overlays opened inside our own sheet or command portal to the ROOT PortalHost and render BEHIND the sheet. Invisible on web, reproduces only on device.
technical_risks.mitigation: Design decision, not an implementation detail: sheet mounts a NAMED PortalHost and passes its name down via context; every RNR overlay rendered inside receives portalHost. Must be specified in the sheet task, because an implementer cannot infer it from the component file.

technical_risks.risk: A hardcoded color or a locally-invented token silently breaks the theming-passthrough contract. Both fail without any error — an unknown Tailwind utility is dropped, and a hex literal simply never re-themes.
technical_risks.mitigation: scripts/check-tokens.ts as a blocking CI job (color-literal grep + token-allowlist check against RNR's published set), plus the six-screenshot token-flip proof on device in light and dark on both platforms. The grep catches the common case; only the device pass catches a color hidden inside a markdown or highlight style object.

technical_risks.risk: A short-name registryDependencies entry resolves against the shadcn WEB registry and installs a DOM component into a React Native app.
technical_risks.mitigation: CI assertion that every registryDependencies entry starts with https://, plus a dependency denylist rejecting any DOM-only package name in a registry item's dependencies. Both are five-line scripts and they eliminate the entire class.

technical_risks.risk: Upstream RNR drift. We reference RNR by live URL, so a future RNR change silently alters what a consumer's add pulls, and our components may stop composing with it.
technical_risks.mitigation: Scheduled CI job that scaffolds the example app fresh from the live RNR registry and typechecks. Document the RNR CLI version we verify against. Vendoring RNR components would pin them but forks the design system and violates constraint 1 — so we accept the drift and detect it instead.

technical_risks.risk: lucide-react-native crossed a major boundary (RNR KB pins ^0.577; npm latest is 1.39.0). Icon export names changed across 0.x->1.x.
technical_risks.mitigation: Pick one version, pin it, and add a typecheck-time barrel that imports every icon the registry uses so a rename fails CI rather than rendering nothing at runtime.

technical_risks.risk: TypeScript 7.0.2 is the new Go-native compiler. Type-testing utilities (expectTypeOf, tsd) and Vitest's typecheck mode may not be fully compatible — which matters because the AI SDK type-conformance test is the primary guard on the one external contract.
technical_risks.mitigation: Prove the conformance test on tsgo in the same task that decides the test runner. Keep typescript@5.9 as a dev-only fallback for that single check if tsgo trips. Do not let a tooling gap become a reason to drop the check.

technical_risks.risk: Android vs iOS keyboard and inset divergence in prompt-input — the single most-used component. Android soft-keyboard behavior differs enough that an iOS-verified implementation regularly ships broken.
technical_risks.mitigation: Core KeyboardAvoidingView with Platform.select behavior in the shipped item (zero dependencies), react-native-keyboard-controller documented as the upgrade. Emulator verification is a required AC for the item, not an optional extra.

technical_risks.risk: Web parity for gesture-driven surfaces — sheet pan-to-dismiss and slider thumb drag have no touch equivalent in a desktop browser.
technical_risks.mitigation: Platform.select the gesture branch off on web and rely on the overlay click-to-dismiss and keyboard arrow handling that @rn-primitives already provides. Constraint: a component that only works on native is not done per AGENTS.md, so web behavior is an AC on both items.

technical_risks.risk: Scope. 49 components + 16 new base primitives + a build system + an example app + a docs site + a test strategy, with prior art whose own maintainer abandoned the RNR-layered approach in his rewrite.
technical_risks.mitigation: Sequence by dependency, not by the alphabet. Wave 1: repo + registry build + one end-to-end component proving the whole pipeline (add from URL into a clean Expo app, renders, themes, passes CI). Wave 2: the shared base primitives everything else composes from (input-group, item, empty, sheet, spinner). Wave 3: the chat shell. Wave 4+: agent, content, and code surfaces. Cut navigation-menu, kbd, and breadcrumb first if a wave slips — nothing in the chat shell depends on them.

technical_risks.risk: Markdown and link rendering is a user-content path: a model-generated javascript: or custom-scheme link, or an oversized/pathological markdown payload.
technical_risks.mitigation: Scheme allowlist (https/http/mailto) before any Linking.openURL, and a length guard on markdown input. Cheap, and it is the kind of thing that is embarrassing to add after shipping.

routing_verdict.reason: Split verdict, and the split is the point. THE LIBRARY HAS NO ROUTES. It is a copy-paste registry of presentational components with no navigator, no linking config, no screen, and no route file — every surface it ships (sheet, command, sidebar, toast, dialog-family overlays) is STATE-driven, opened by a prop or a ref, not by navigation. Writing a route map for the registry would be a category error, and worse, it would invite an implementer to reach for expo-router inside a component and couple the library to a navigator its consumers may not use. THE EXAMPLE APP HAS ROUTES, and they are real deliverables: apps/example uses expo-router with a root _layout.tsx (Uniwind provider + ThemeProvider + RNR <PortalHost /> as the last child + our <Toaster />), a chat screen, a component-gallery index with one route per registry item (this doubles as the device-verification surface and the docs site via expo export -p web), and the app/api/chat+api.ts server route. A Route Delta therefore applies to apps/example only. One routing-adjacent rule that DOES bind the library: because the consumer owns the navigator, our components must never assume one — no useRouter, no Link, no useNavigation in any registry file. Anything navigational is an onPress callback the consumer wires.
